mcp.summary: The video delivers a polished nighttime launch and racing exchange with the supplied dialogue, but the finish is undermined by duplicated cars and contradictory travel directions that obscure the winner.

must_haves.item: A starter counts down 'three, two, one, go' at the start line, audibly, at the beginning.
must_haves.why: A starter stands between the staged cars, and the supplied transcript confirms the exact countdown at 0–4 seconds.

must_haves.item: Two modified cars launch from the line and race.
must_haves.why: The modified red and blue cars are staged together, advance past the starter, and appear racing alongside each other.

must_haves.item: During the race each driver shouts one short line to the other, audibly, over the engines.
must_haves.why: The transcript supplies two short racing taunts at 9–10 and 11–12 seconds, matching the respective car close-ups; the blue driver visibly shouts, but speaker attribution for the red car and audibility over engines are not fully verifiable.

must_haves.item: It ends on the winner crossing the finish.
must_haves.why: The red car crosses a checkered road marking near 13 seconds, but the final frame shows additional red-car imagery and opposing car orientations, making the winner and closing action inconsistent.
The frames consistently depict a lit urban street at night in 16:9, and the supplied timing establishes a 16-second video.

v3-race-1.summary: A visually coherent nighttime street race delivers the exact opening countdown and two short taunts, but lacks a visible starter, clearly modified cars, verified driver-to-driver dialogue, and an unambiguous winning finish.

must_haves.item: A starter counts down 'three, two, one, go' at the start line, audibly, at the beginning.
must_haves.why: The transcript confirms the exact countdown at 0–2.5 seconds, with two cars staged side by side, but no starter or clearly marked start line is visible.

must_haves.item: Two modified cars launch from the line and race.
must_haves.why: The red and silver cars advance together and race side by side, but a distinct launch is weakly established and substantial modifications are not clearly visible.

must_haves.item: During the race each driver shouts one short line to the other, audibly, over the engines.
must_haves.why: The transcript supplies 'Keep up!' and 'Not tonight!' during the race, but the frames do not establish that each driver delivers one to the other; engine sound and vocal delivery cannot be verified from the transcript.

must_haves.item: It ends on the winner crossing the finish.
must_haves.why: The red car passes a transverse white road marking near 13 seconds, but it is not clearly identified as the finish or shown decisively winning; the final frame instead shows it driving away.
The frames consistently show a lamp-lit industrial street at night in 16:9, and the supplied duration is 16 seconds.

v3-race-1 vs mcp.why: The first video better matches the brief with a visible starter, clearly modified cars, separately timed driver taunts, and a marked finish-line crossing, although its final shot has continuity glitches. The second includes the countdown and racing dialogue but lacks a visible starter and ends with cars driving away rather than a clearly identifiable winner crossing the finish.
